documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiac surgery service
Admitted 05/14/2024. Discharged 05/26/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Procedures: emergent cardiac catheterization with reperfusion of the culprit lesion; coronary artery bypass grafting, multivessel (05/19/2024).

Course: 68-year-old man with CAD (MIs 2014 and 2018, stent 2014), HFrEF, type 2 diabetes, COPD and a seizure disorder, who woke with crushing chest pain and arrived by ambulance with ST elevation on ECG. Taken directly to the cath lab; the culprit was reperfused and catheterization showed multivessel disease. Heart team recommended surgical revascularization, performed on hospital day 6. Post-operative course without major complication; extubated on schedule, chest tubes removed, ambulating the halls before discharge. No seizures during the stay; valproic acid continued.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, lisinopril 20 daily, furosemide 20 daily, metformin 1000 twice daily, insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, valproic acid 500 twice daily, albuterol as needed, nitroglycerin SL as needed.
Follow-up: cardiothoracic surgery in 3 days; cardiology in 4-6 weeks; PCP within 1-2 weeks; outpatient cardiac rehabilitation referral placed.
Sternal precautions: no lifting over 10 lb, no driving for 4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Median sternotomy wires intact and aligned. Small left pleural effusion with blunting of the left costophrenic angle. No pneumothorax. No focal consolidation. Cardiac silhouette enlarged, as before.
reports.conclusion: Small left pleural effusion after CABG.

documents.author: cardiothoracic surgery

Outside cardiothoracic surgery group
Date of visit: 05/29/2024

Seen three days after discharge following CABG for his STEMI. Background of prior MIs, heart failure and diabetic neuropathy. No chest pain. Some breathlessness with exertion that he did not have before the operation. No fever, chills or cough. Incisions bother him a little at night.
Medications: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, insulin glargine 24 units qHS, valproic acid 500 BID, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 135/85, HR 78, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air.
Lungs: breath sounds decreased at the left base, no wheezes or crackles. Sternal and leg incisions healing, no drainage. Rest of exam unremarkable.
Chest X-ray: small left pleural effusion.

Assessment: recovering after CABG; small left effusion, common after this surgery.
Plan: observe, incentive spirometer, walking. Repeat chest X-ray in 4 weeks. Sternal precautions continue. Start cardiac rehab when cleared.

Cardiothoracic Surgery

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit here since his STEMI and bypass. Discharge summary and surgery note reviewed. Wife drove.
No chest pain. Winded on the stairs, a little better each day; surgeon is watching a small fluid collection on the left. Incisions sore at night. Med rec done against bottles: aspirin, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, furosemide 20, metformin, glargine 24, valproic acid, albuterol, NTG. Cardiac rehab intake next week.
Mood: low since the hospital. Not sleeping, doesn't enjoy much, sits in the chair a lot. PHQ-9 14. No thoughts of harming himself. Says he feels like his body betrayed him.
Exam: tired-appearing. Sternotomy clean, healing. Heart regular. Breath sounds reduced at the left base. Trace ankle edema. Leg harvest site fine.
A/P:
1. STEMI s/p CABG, recovering. Meds unchanged from discharge. Rehab, sternal precautions. Cardiology and surgery follow-ups booked.
2. Left effusion post-op, surgeon following.
3. Depressive symptoms after the MI, PHQ-9 14. Common after heart surgery and worth treating. Referral to psychiatry; he prefers a specialist. Crisis line given.
4. HFrEF, T2DM: continue. BMP today on the furosemide.
RTC after psychiatry and rehab start.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Comparison 05/29/2024. Sternotomy wires intact. Left costophrenic angle now sharp; the small left effusion has resolved. Lungs clear. No pneumothorax. Heart size unchanged.

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient behavioral health
Date of service: 07/11/2024

Referred by PCP. 68-year-old retired foreman seen about six weeks after a hospital stay for STEMI, treated with emergent catheterization and then bypass surgery. Prior MIs 2014 and 2018; heart failure. Discharged on aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin and lisinopril with his other medicines; taking them as directed and going to cardiac rehab three times a week.
Since the hospital: sadness most days, no interest in the workshop or the ballgames he used to follow, broken sleep, about 5 lb of weight loss, tired all the time. Denies suicidal thoughts, intent or plan. No prior depressive episodes or psychiatric care. No mania. Sober from alcohol since 2019.
Medical: CAD, HFrEF, T2DM on insulin with neuropathy, HTN, HLD, COPD, complex partial seizures on valproic acid.
Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals within normal limits. Exam unremarkable.
MSE: casually dressed, cooperative, slowed, mood 'down', affect constricted, thought process linear, no SI/HI, insight and judgment fair.
Recent labs (07/02/2024): Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.0, fasting glucose 98, total cholesterol 175, LDL 70, HDL 45.

Assessment: major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate, after acute MI.
Plan: sertraline 25 mg daily for a week, then 50 mg; well studied after heart attacks. Discussed aspirin and bleeding risk with SSRIs; no NSAIDs. Brief supportive therapy here. Return 6-8 weeks. Safety plan reviewed; wife aware.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department
Date of visit: 12/11/2025

CC: three days of right heel-cord pain, can't put weight on it.
HPI: 70M with CAD s/p CABG, HFrEF, insulin-treated T2DM with neuropathy, depression followed by psychiatry since his 2024 STEMI, and a prior right foot ulcer seen by podiatry. Three days ago, walking down a flight of stairs, felt a sudden sharp stabbing pain at the back of the right ankle, worse with any motion, with a clicking sensation near the heel. No fall or blow, no fever, no swelling elsewhere. Started ciprofloxacin 5 days ago at urgent care for a UTI; no steroid use.
He also says his mood has slid badly over the last month since his mother was told she has metastatic small cell lung cancer. Feels helpless and guilty, tired, sleeping through the day, skipping meals, has stopped going to the senior center. Admits he's been missing doses of his medicines. Denies suicidal ideation. His sister keeps pushing him to sign estate papers while their mother is still on chemo, and the calls leave him overwhelmed; he's been letting them go to voicemail. Had a video visit with his PCP yesterday for refills and didn't mention the ankle.
PMH: CAD with MIs 2014, 2018 and 05/2024 STEMI, CABG 2024, stent 2014; HFrEF; T2DM; HTN; HLD; COPD; complex partial seizures on valproic acid; MDD.
Meds: metoprolol, atorvastatin, lisinopril, aspirin, metformin, valproic acid, insulin glargine, albuterol PRN, ciprofloxacin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 40 pack-years. Former heavy whiskey drinker, 2-3 a night, none since 2019.
Family: mother with metastatic small cell lung cancer.

Vitals: T 36.9 C, P 72, RR 14, BP 136/82.
Exam: looks older than his years, no distress. Antalgic gait, favoring the left. Right posterior ankle just above the heel: mild swelling and point tenderness; tendon thicker than the left. Thompson test: plantar flexion diminished with calf squeeze. Passive dorsiflexion sharply painful. Plantar flexion weak. No redness, warmth or crepitus. Sensation and pulses intact.
Labs: WBC, ESR and CRP normal.
X-ray right ankle: mild degenerative change, no fracture or calcification.

Impression: right Achilles tendinopathy with suspected rupture, likely from the fluoroquinolone.
Plan: stop ciprofloxacin; cephalexin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days to finish the UTI course. Walking boot with heel lift, crutches, no weight bearing until seen. Orthopedics referral, appointment within the week. Acetaminophen for pain, avoid NSAIDs with his heart failure. Avoid fluoroquinolones in future. Worsening depression: no SI, safe for discharge with his wife; encouraged to call his psychiatrist and PCP this week. Return for calf swelling, chest pain or thoughts of self-harm.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his ED visit. In the boot, on crutches, wife with him. Ortho on Friday. Ankle pain easing at rest. Finished the cephalexin, no more urinary symptoms.
Mood is the bigger issue. His mother's cancer diagnosis last month hit hard, plus a lot of conflict with his sister over the estate. Sleeping days, not eating much, down 2 kg since September. Has missed doses, mostly evening ones, glargine included some nights. PHQ-9 15. Denies thoughts of suicide or self-harm, no plan, no weapons in the house; wife confirms.
Exam: tired, flat. Regular, lungs clear, no edema. Right Achilles thickened and tender, in boot.
A/P:
1. Right Achilles tendinopathy, suspected rupture, after ciprofloxacin. Boot, crutches, ortho Friday. Ciprofloxacin added to the allergy list as an intolerance; no fluoroquinolones going forward.
2. MDD, worse with family stressors, PHQ-9 15, no SI. Sent a message to his psychiatrist today asking for an earlier visit; they'll call him. Safety plan reviewed. Weekly check-in calls from our RN until then.
3. Missed doses: pillbox set up with wife; he agreed to let her help with the evening ones.
4. UTI resolved.
5. Other chronic issues unchanged.

conditions.label: Spontaneous rupture of other tendons, right lower leg
conditions.note: high-grade partial tear of the right Achilles tendon after ciprofloxacin

documents.title: Orthopedics consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic group
Date of visit: 12/19/2025

Seen from the ED for right Achilles pain that began on stairs on 12/08 while on ciprofloxacin, with a diminished Thompson test there.
Allergies: ciprofloxacin (tendon injury).
Exam: tendon thickened and tender just above the insertion, no palpable gap. Thompson test with reduced but present plantar flexion. Weak push-off. Sensation intact, foot warm, pulses present.
Ultrasound in clinic: high-grade partial-thickness tear of the right Achilles tendon. Fibers in continuity; no complete rupture.

Assessment: high-grade partial tear of the right Achilles tendon, fluoroquinolone-associated.
Plan: nonoperative care, which suits him given his heart history and diabetic foot. Walking boot with heel wedges, protected weight bearing as tolerated, wedges removed in stages over 6-8 weeks. Physical therapy referral. No fluoroquinolones in future. Recheck in the spring, sooner if pain or weakness worsens.

Orthopedics
